name: feigenbaum-kantorovich-preflight
authority: Research 0129 section 3; this contract authorizes one bounded run and nothing else, and it is written as a preflight because one required bound is not available
question: Which of the quantities a Newton-Kantorovich test needs for the Feigenbaum fixed point can be computed rigorously here, and which are still missing?
level: External exact rational algebra on a frozen candidate: an exact polynomial defect, an exact weighted norm, a verified inverse bound for a truncated linearisation, and an explicit preflight obstruction for the infinite-dimensional conclusion
domain: Even power series G(y) = sum a_j y^j with a_0 = 1 solving G = T[G] for T[G](y) = A G((G(y/A^2))^2), A = 1/G(1); the weighted l1 norm ||G||_rho = sum |a_j| rho^j with a declared rho; a candidate frozen as an exact rational vector; the linearisation computed analytically, not by differencing

objects.degree_note: the exact rational composition is the cost driver; these degrees keep the run inside its budget and the defect it measures is the truncation defect at that degree
objects.rho_note: rho must lie inside the convergence radius of the series; with rho = 1/4 the weighted norm of the candidate exceeds any reasonable image radius and the hypothesis fails, which the first run showed and which is recorded rather than hidden

quantifiers: Every coefficient of the exact defect polynomial up to the declared defect degree
Every entry of the truncated linearisation matrix, computed analytically
Every reported bound compared against the exact rational value it bounds
acceptance: The candidate is frozen as an exact rational vector and the defect d = x0 - T[x0] is computed exactly as a rational polynomial, because composing polynomials gives a polynomial
The weighted norm of the defect is exact, and it is reported with its exact numerator size rather than as a decimal alone
The disk-mapping hypothesis that licenses composition bounds is checked from the coefficients and shown to hold for the candidate and to fail for a scaled copy
A truncated linearisation is assembled analytically in exact rationals and its inverse is verified by the residual criterion ||I - M X|| < 1, which then bounds ||M^-1||
A perturbed candidate is shown to have a larger defect, so the defect check is not vacuous
The missing bounds are enumerated, and no enclosure of alpha or delta is claimed, because the tail bound on the inverse is absent
protected: The four earlier Feigenbaum rounds are frozen and are not rewritten
The truncated inverse bound is not presented as the inverse bound of the full operator
No existence or uniqueness of the fixed point is claimed
The exact defect of a truncated polynomial is not presented as the defect of an exact solution
No metric, Arakelov, Monge-Ampere, mirror or Calabi-Yau content is introduced
No native Rust witness, library admission or Seal follows from this calibration
residual: This supplies the defect exactly, the disk-mapping hypothesis and a verified inverse bound for a truncation, and it names the two bounds a Kantorovich test still needs: the tail bound on the inverse of the linearised operator and a bound on its second derivative. The trial is therefore not launched, and no enclosure of alpha or delta follows. The candidate is a frozen rational approximation, so its defect is the defect of that approximation and not of an exact solution.
